rules.rule: If comparing text at the same point size, measure the x-height (height of lowercase letters without ascenders or descenders) to determine which appears bigger.
rules.evidence: What your eyes are actually measuring is the x-height: the height of a lowercase letter that has no ascender and no descender.

rules.rule: If evaluating legibility at small sizes, check for high stroke contrast and tight apertures, as these features tend to fail below one pixel.
rules.evidence: High contrast, tight apertures and delicate terminals look superb at 60px and turn to mush at 11px: the thin strokes fall below one pixel and the apertures fill in.

rules.rule: If distinguishing typeface from font, identify the design as the typeface and the specific file (e.g., Helvetica-Bold.otf) as the font.
rules.evidence: A typeface is the design. A font is the file.

rules.rule: If analyzing italic style, verify if letters are redrawn with cursive structure rather than mechanically slanted to avoid identifying it as a faux italic.
rules.evidence: True italics are redrawn from cursive structure; the a and g usually change shape entirely. A mechanically slanted roman is an oblique at best.
